position: the outset, via `l4 lts --contract receipts`: nothing has happened; clock 0
questions: Q1. What is owed right now, and by whom?
Q2. Which event(s) would discharge what is owed?
Q3. Which event(s) or deadline(s) would put someone in breach?
Q4. Where in the contract are we — which rule, branch or state is live?
Q5. What happens after the next discharging event?
truth: Each of the three tenants — Alice, Bob and Carol — MUST Pay the landlord (Ms Ng), each due by day 7. The amount is not fixed by the rule. The landlord owes nothing yet.

Each tenant paying the landlord on or before day 7 discharges that tenant's own payment obligation (any amount, even 0 — the rule binds the amount, it does not test it; paying someone other than the landlord does not count). The contract as a whole ends FULFILLED only when all three have paid and the landlord has issued all three receipts.

The clock passing day 7 with a tenant unpaid: if nothing happens by 7 (the clock reaches 8) there is a breach, which the evaluator names to Alice (the first member whose deadline passed; a tenant paying late at 8 is likewise a breach named to Alice). Later, a landlord who does not issue a receipt within 5 days of a payment is in breach.
At the start: the EVERY fork (`UPON EACH`), three parallel branches, one per tenant, none of which has acted. No receipt obligation exists yet.

When one tenant pays (say Alice at day 3), the landlord MUST issue Alice a receipt for that amount within 5 days (by day 8); the other two tenants still owe their payments by day 7. A receipt in time closes Alice's branch; no receipt by 8 puts the landlord in breach. Each tenant's branch runs on its own.
